item.title: Goshiki-numa: The Five Colour Ponds of Urabandai — Guide
item.description: Goshiki-numa, the ‘Five Colour Ponds’, is a chain of volcanic lakes on the northern side of Mount Bandai, formed when the 1888 eruption dammed local rivers and created dozens of ponds across the Urabandai plateau. Mineral content and depth give each pond its own distinct hue — from cobalt blue to jade green to milky turquoise — best appreciated on the roughly 3.6 km walking trail that links the main ponds, part of the wider Bandai Highland Lakes region of forested trails and mountain scenery.

item.title: Fukushima Nature: Bandai Volcanic Highland, Goshiki-numa Lakes & Flower Country
item.description: Fukushima Prefecture Nature & Outdoor Guide Fukushima Prefecture, stretching from the Pacific coast to the central mountains of Honshu, offers some of Japan’s most dramatic volcanic landscapes, pristine forests, and accessible highland trails. Despite lingering misconceptions, the prefecture’s natural areas are safe, spectacular, and surprisingly uncrowded—making them ideal for international visitors seeking authentic Japanese nature experiences away from the tourist crowds. 1. Bandai-Asahi National Park & Mount Bandai (磐梯朝日国立公園・磐梯山) The catastrophic eruption of Mount Bandai in 1888 transformed the landscape forever, creating over 300 lakes and ponds across what is now known as the Urabandai (Back-Bandai) highland.

item.title: Top Sightseeing in Fukushima: Aizu Castle, Ouchi-juku & Five-Colour Lakes
item.description: Discovering Fukushima Prefecture: A Complete Sightseeing Guide Often overlooked by international travelers racing between Tokyo and northern Tohoku, Fukushima Prefecture offers some of Japan’s most authentic historical experiences, dramatic natural landscapes, and poignant cultural stories. From samurai castles to volcanic lakes, from preserved Edo-period villages to massive limestone caverns, Fukushima rewards those who venture beyond the typical tourist trail. Getting to Fukushima Fukushima Prefecture is highly accessible from major cities. The JR Tohoku Shinkansen connects Tokyo Station to Koriyama Station in just 80 minutes, making it an easy addition to any Japan itinerary.
